title: dedicated: priority-aware autoscaler + burst controls + utilization reporting enhancements
author: Aisha Patel
description: Context: Customers running mixed-priority workloads on Dedicated fleets saw priority inversion and noisy-neighbor style bursts that violated per-tenant throughput guarantees. This PR implements a priority-aware autoscaler, tighter burst controls (token-bucket smoothing + per-priority burst budgets), and improved utilization reporting surfaced to the Console. Motivation: reduce P99 latency regressions during bursts, ensure priority SLAs, and give SREs visibility into priority-level utilization trends. Changes: 1) Autoscaler: new priority-aware scoring that weights recent queueing latency and burst budget consumption; supports per-priority min/max pool targets and a priority preemption hint for fast reclaim. 2) Burst controls: token-bucket smoothing applied per-priority with configurable refill_rate and burst_budget window; added safeguards to avoid thrashing (predictive cooldown). 3) Utilization reporting: new metrics redwood.dedicated.fleet.utilization.by_priority and redwood.dedicated.fleet.burst_budget.used; rollups for 1m/5m/1h; added dashboard tiles and alert rules. 4) API/Config: expose new fields in fleet config (priority_policies, burst_policy) with validation and migration path. 5) Tests/Docs: integration tests for preemption and smoothing, unit tests for tokenbucket edgecases, updated Dedicated docs and changelog. Rollout plan: gated feature flag, canary on 2 fleets, monitor utilization and latency dashboards; automatic rollback on >3% P99 latency regression per canary. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration test harness updates - [x] Console dashboard updates - [x] Docs and migration notes - [x] Manual canary run completed

review_comments: Luca Moretti: Nice design; can we add a short note about eventual consistency between metrics rollups and the scaler decision window? Author reply: yes — addressed by adding a 30s alignment window to the scorer and documenting it.

Jasmine Lee: Concerned about preemption safety for long-running jobs — please ensure preemption only affects new requests not in-progress tokens. Author reply: preemption sends a soft-reclaim hint; in-progress tokens are honored, added e2e to verify.

Diego Ramirez: We saw flakiness in tokenbucket tests when clock jumps occur. Suggest using mocked monotonic clock. Author reply: switched to monotonic clock in tests and added time-jump regression test.
CI Bot: integration/dedicated-tests failed on first run (race in tokenbucket); fix pushed and rerun shows green.
QA: Please include instructions for forcing priority buckets on canary fleets for testing — added helper script in scripts/ci.
Security: config validation looks good; recommend adding max limits for burst_budget to avoid accidental OOM — applied conservative upper bounds.
Jasmine Lee: Approving after fixes — LGTM.
release_notes: Improved dedicated autoscaling with priority-aware scaling; per-priority burst smoothing and token-bucket budgets to reduce latency spikes; new utilization metrics by priority and updated Console dashboards; migration path for fleet configs. Configuration note: add priority_policies and burst_policy to fleet config; a migration script is provided.
